messages:
maya: Quick check — after merging the paged-attn changes (PR #542) I'm seeing a cold-start latency regression on long sequences (~8k). Can someone run the microbench on a prod-like instance? repro and desired measurements below.

sam: I can run it. Which image/config and which pool? Also paste the exact bench command.

maya: gpu-pool-a (A100-80GB), image: inference:v3.4. Use bench/micro/bench_attn.py with these flags: `--model llama-13b --seq 8192 --batch 1 --warmup 50 --iters 200 --prefetch-kv true` — measure first-token latency vs steady-state. Note: we changed the fusion path for softmax+scale in this PR.

devon: grabbing a node now. Will run baseline (pre-PR) and head. ETA ~12m.

infra-bot: Scheduled job 1830076890: microbench/gpu-pool-a (A100-80GB) started by devon. Docker image: inference:v3.4.

devon: Baseline (commit a1f9d8c) results: FIRST_TOKEN=138ms, STEADY=39ms.

devon: Head (commit b3c4e2f + PR #542) results: FIRST_TOKEN=228ms, STEADY=43ms. So steady-state is fine, cold-start regressed ~+90ms. Minimal log: ```[baseline] first=138ms steady=39ms
[head] first=228ms steady=43ms```

sam: Interesting — steady-state similar, so KV/cache behavior fine. Cold-start +90ms suggests extra compile or heavyweight init on the fused path. Any GPU JIT or kernel compile messages in dmesg or runtime logs?

ryan: My hunch: the new fused softmax kernel triggers a dynamic kernel specialization on first long-seq run. That can compile NVRTC code or load a new kernel into the driver, causing the one-off hit. Two quick mitigations to try: 1) enable runtime kernel cache before requests `export RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_CACHE=1` and warm it, or 2) pre-warm by running a short dummy request at startup (we already do warmup=50 but that might not exercise the specialized path).

maya: Good call. Can you try 1) with kernel cache on, and 2) also run bench with a short pre-warm call that uses full seq length before measuring?

devon: Ran two quick variants on same node:
- head + RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_CACHE=0 + normal warmup => FIRST=228ms
- head + RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_CACHE=1 + explicit prewarm (single request seq=8192 before measuring) => FIRST=152ms
So kernel cache cuts the regression to ~+14ms vs baseline. Logs: ```cache=off first=228ms
cache=on prewarm first=152ms```

sam: OK that strongly points at kernel load/compile on cold-start. We should: A) enable kernel cache by default on the runtime for dedicated/hosted pools, B) add an optional prewarm hook that the deploy config can toggle, and C) add a small telemetry event for "kernel_cache_miss" on first-run so we can measure frequency. Thoughts?

elaine: Filed infra ticket INF-2042 to enable RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_CACHE in staging pools and added a canary rollout plan. I'll put a canary on 10% of dedicated nodes for 24h. cc @sam @maya :white_check_mark:

ryan: Agreed on telemetry. Also let's add a short note in the PR about the compile behavior — helps reviewers know this is expected trade-off. Could also investigate making the fused kernel less dynamic (more permutations baked in) to avoid runtime specialization.

maya: Thanks all. Action items: sam to add kernel-cache toggle + telemetry (small PR), elaine to roll canary, devon to run a quick prewarm on deployment images, ryan to add PR note. I'll follow up tomorrow with perf dashboards. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Job 1830076890 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/microbench/1830076890/{baseline,head}/logs.txt

sam: Ping me if you want me to draft the PR, I can include a short integration test that runs one long-seq prewarm in CI.

maya: Please do. That test can live in tests/e2e/warmup_smoke.py. Short and flaky-safe.

devon: Leaving node; saved profiles to the artifact bucket. Will retest after canary is live.

elaine: Canary scheduled for 10% on dedicated starting 18:30 PT. I'll post results in #eng-runtime.

maya: Great teamwork — closing the loop after telemetry shows reduction.
